premises: *capalam asi yad api mānasa.* Mind, though fickle — even so you are praised, since you worship the refuge of refuges, the world's teacher, Ambikā's husband. Fickleness forgiven for direction: praise for turning, not for steadiness. (Lakshmanjoo addresses his own mind throughout.)
reconstruction: *capalam asi yad api mānasa.* Mind, though fickle — even so you are praised, since you worship the refuge of refuges, the world's teacher, Ambikā's husband. Fickleness forgiven for direction: praise for turning, not for steadiness. (Lakshmanjoo addresses his own mind throughout.)

premises: *ullaṅghya vividhadaivatasopānakramam.* Having crossed the ladder-steps of various gods, reached Śiva's feet — yet on the lowest ground I stand even now; wonder, I do not quit it. Arrival without departure: highest object, lowest seat, no contradiction felt.
reconstruction: *ullaṅghya vividhadaivatasopānakramam.* Having crossed the ladder-steps of various gods, reached Śiva's feet — yet on the lowest ground I stand even now; wonder, I do not quit it. Arrival without departure: highest object, lowest seat, no contradiction felt.

premises: *prakaṭaya nijam adhvānaṃ sthagayatarām.* Reveal Your own path, hide all world-ways thoroughly — while I am, Lord, quickly Your ever-risen servant. Double imperative: show Yours, cover theirs; use me now (*sapadi*).
reconstruction: *prakaṭaya nijam adhvānaṃ sthagayatarām.* Reveal Your own path, hide all world-ways thoroughly — while I am, Lord, quickly Your ever-risen servant. Double imperative: show Yours, cover theirs; use me now (*sapadi*).

premises: *śiva śiva śambho śaṅkara.* Śiva Śiva Śambhu Śaṅkara — swift pity on the refuge-seekers' lover! Fortune is near for whoever remembers Your lotus-feet-pair. Name-piling as spell; mercy as speed (*āśu*).
reconstruction: *śiva śiva śambho śaṅkara.* Śiva Śiva Śambhu Śaṅkara — swift pity on the refuge-seekers' lover! Fortune is near for whoever remembers Your lotus-feet-pair. Name-piling as spell; mercy as speed (*āśu*).

premises: *tāvakāṅghrikamalāsanalīnā.* Those seated on Your foot-lotus-throne, making the world to taste — they laugh at Vir iñc (Brahmā), office-stained, not-self-ruled. Devotees laugh at the creator: office (*adhikāra*) stains, throne-sitting frees.
reconstruction: *tāvakāṅghrikamalāsanalīnā.* Those seated on Your foot-lotus-throne, making the world to taste — they laugh at Vir iñc (Brahmā), office-stained, not-self-ruled. Devotees laugh at the creator: office (*adhikāra*) stains, throne-sitting frees.

premises: *tvatprakāśavapuṣo na vibhinnaṃ kiṃ cana.* Nothing appears apart from Your light-body; so You are always already gained, Lord — though far by nature. Immanence proved, transcendence kept: gained AND far.
reconstruction: *tvatprakāśavapuṣo na vibhinnaṃ kiṃ cana.* Nothing appears apart from Your light-body; so You are always already gained, Lord — though far by nature. Immanence proved, transcendence kept: gained AND far.

premises: *pādapaṅkajarasaṃ tava ke cid.* Some taste Your foot-lotus-juice as stale-difference-conduct; others instantly taste it as flawless, body-whole, duality-free. Two tastes, one dust: stale vs fresh is the taster's, not the foot's.
reconstruction: *pādapaṅkajarasaṃ tava ke cid.* Some taste Your foot-lotus-juice as stale-difference-conduct; others instantly taste it as flawless, body-whole, duality-free. Two tastes, one dust: stale vs fresh is the taster's, not the foot's.

premises: *nātha vidyud iva bhāti vibhāte.* Lord, like lightning at dawn gleams my nectar-smeared — if it stayed steadier, You are worshipped duly — what else? Flash-devotion: one steady flash would complete all rite. (Conditional worship: *if* it stayed.)
reconstruction: *nātha vidyud iva bhāti vibhāte.* Lord, like lightning at dawn gleams my nectar-smeared — if it stayed steadier, You are worshipped duly — what else? Flash-devotion: one steady flash would complete all rite. (Conditional worship: *if* it stayed.)

premises: *sarvam asyaparam asti na kiṃ cid.* Is there anything, thing or non-thing, apart from this? With great discernment decided here: as You are, so be plain to me. Discernment (*prajñā*) issues in demand: appear as You are.
reconstruction: *sarvam asyaparam asti na kiṃ cid.* Is there anything, thing or non-thing, apart from this? With great discernment decided here: as You are, so be plain to me. Discernment (*prajñā*) issues in demand: appear as You are.

premises: *svecchayaiva bhagavan nijamārge kāritaḥ padam.* By Your will alone, Lord, I was made to step on Your own path — then why do I behave just like a man, knowing nothing fit for Your feet? Placed unasked (Lakshmanjoo's stressed point: "I never asked You... You have done it Yourself!"), yet behaving humanly — the complaint of the carried.

premises: *ko 'pi deva hṛdi teṣu tāvako jṛmbhate.* Some god of Yours blooms in their hearts, a lovely supreme state — by whose story-thunder-cātakas they are long gladdened. Devotion blooms unasked in some; story-rain gladdens long.
reconstruction: *ko 'pi deva hṛdi teṣu tāvako jṛmbhate.* Some god of Yours blooms in their hearts, a lovely supreme state — by whose story-thunder-cātakas they are long gladdened. Devotion blooms unasked in some; story-rain gladdens long.

premises: *tvajjuṣāṃ tvayi kayāpi līlayā rāga eṣa paripoṣam āgataḥ.* For Your devotees, by some play in You, this love has grown fat — so that separation-ground talk and memory fruit in union-festival. Play grows love; separation-talk (*saṅkathā*) itself fruits in union.

premises: *yo vicitrarasasekavardhitaḥ.* The word, grown by strange-rasa-sprinkling, though uttered "Śaṅkara" hundreds of times — enters even sideways hearts, ever-fresh in purpose. The Name penetrates the unwilling; freshness never stales.

premises: *te jayanti mukhamaṇḍale bhraman.* Victorious are they on whose face-orbits the Śiva-sound ever revolves — which, moon-spread from nectar-source, trickles supreme nectar, sweet. Faces win: sound on the mouth beats thought in the head.

premises: *parisamāptam ivogram idaṃ jagad.* The fierce world as if finished; mind's impurity thinned to none — and yet not even the smallest knocking at Your city-door-bolt. End of differentiation (Lakshmanjoo's Bruce Hughes passage) — yet no entry knocked. The door verse: realization without arrival. Do not resolve.

premises: *satataphullabhavanmukhapaṅkajodaravilokanalālasacetasaḥ.* Of minds eager for Your ever-blooming face-lotus-belly-gaze — do something, Lord, just a little, so You flash as facing me. "Just a little" (*manāg iva*): the smallest turn asked.

premises: *tvadavibhedamater aparaṃ nu kiṃ sukham.* What happiness here apart from non-difference-mind, what other glory? So why does this servant's mind, abandoning her, go the wrong way?

premises: *kṣaṇam apīha na tāvakadāsatāṃ prati.* May I never for a moment be unfit for Your serfdom — unless constantly, reverently tasting non-difference-wine. Fitness redefined as tasting-frequency.
reconstruction: *kṣaṇam apīha na tāvakadāsatāṃ prati.* May I never for a moment be unfit for Your serfdom — unless constantly, reverently tasting non-difference-wine. Fitness redefined as tasting-frequency.

premises: *na kila paśyati satyam ayaṃ janas.* These people truly do not see Your body, dirtied by duality-sight — and yet, all-knowing refuge-lover, do You not hear MY cry? Others' blindness conceded; his cry excepted. (Lakshmanjoo: "I confess it, my Lord.")

premises: *smarasi nātha kadācid apīhitaṃ* Do You remember, Lord, any desired sense-pleasure I ever asked? Give instead, always, Your body-vision-nectar as the only wish. Pleasures recalled only to be exchanged.
reconstruction: *smarasi nātha kadācid apīhitaṃ* Do You remember, Lord, any desired sense-pleasure I ever asked? Give instead, always, Your body-vision-nectar as the only wish. Pleasures recalled only to be exchanged.

premises: *kila yadaiva śivādhvani tāvake kṛtapado 'smi.* Since by Your will alone I stepped on Your Śiva-path, Lord — hundreds of good omens rose for me; what else should I seek from You? Placed-ness (10) returns as contentment. (Lakshmanjoo: hundreds of good things.)

premises: *apy upārjitam ahaṃ triṣu lokeṣv adhipatyam.* Even won rule in three worlds, O king of gods, I count tasteless — lacking Your foot-touch-nectar-rasa. Empire vs foot-touch: no contest.

premises: *bata nātha dṛḍho 'yam ātmabandho.* Alas, Lord, strong is this self-bond, made of non-recognition of You, fashioned by You alone — first ignored by me, it never loosens a bit. Bond made BY Him OF non-recognition: akhyāti is the Pratyabhijñā technical term (failure to recognize the Self), not fame. The knot He tied. Held, not solved.

premises: *mahatām amareśa pūjyamāno 'py.* Though worshipped by the great, O king of gods, You ever stay the one-worshipper-form — seen outside and in, You shine in the seers' bodies forever. Final inversion: the worshipped is the worshipper; He shines inside the seers, not above them.
